key_insight: Off-the-shelf image-to-image generative models can reliably remove or overwrite imperceptible protective perturbations, allowing attackers to bypass image protection schemes without specialized, purpose-built attacks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses whether existing image protection techniques (which add subtle perturbations to prevent misuse like style mimicry or deepfakes) remain effective when confronted with widely available image-to-image GenAI models.
method: Repurpose standard image-to-image generative models (plug-and-play) as restoration/transformation pipelines to neutralize protective perturbations.
Apply these models with minimal or no task-specific engineering to protected images to produce visually similar but protection-free outputs.
Evaluate applicability across common protection strategies to show broad effectiveness of off-the-shelf approaches.
impact: This work shows many current image-protection schemes are fragile against readily available GenAI tools, forcing practitioners to rethink defense designs, threat models, and deployment practices to protect image assets and deter misuse.
visual_elements: Before/After image pair: protected image (with imperceptible perturbation) vs output after off-the-shelf image-to-image model.
Pipeline diagram: protected image -> off-the-shelf image-to-image model (no fine-tuning) -> unprotected output.
Bar chart or matrix: comparative effectiveness — off-the-shelf models vs specialized attacks across multiple protection types.
Risk iconography: simple infographic showing stakeholders affected (creators, platforms, model developers) and recommended next steps (harden defenses, update threat models).
paper_title: Off-The-Shelf Image-to-Image Models Are All You Need To Defeat Image Protection Schemes
paper_authors: Xavier Pleimling, Sifat Muhammad Abdullah, Gunjan Balde, Peng Gao, Mainack Mondal
